label: om-brainstorm - talk an idea through before anything is built
text:
<the idea, question or itch - what you noticed and why it might matter>

No flags. Ask one open question at a time and wait for the answer; never batch them.
Weigh building nothing as a real option, and check docs/agents/out-of-scope.md before shaping one:
a request listed there is not re-litigated. Stay read-only on the repository apart from the handoff
brief. End with a `Next:` line - usually `om-prepare-issue` or `om-spec-writing` - and say what the
decision rests on.

label: om-discover - build the product brief every later skill reads
text:
<the product, area or idea to discover>

Flags: --mode existing|client|own · --refresh (update, superseding decisions, never deleting) ·
--research <dir> (default .ai/specs/research) · --quick (one bounded round).
Work only from material that exists - tag every claim with its evidence and give every decision an
owner. Invent nothing. Writes .ai/specs/product-brief.md, whose Non-goals, Business rules and
Decisions tables become a protected contract (SDLC.md). docs/plans/ is the existing backlog source
and docs/adr/ the existing decision record: read both before adding a claim.

label: om-prepare-issue - file one well-formed issue, implement nothing
text:
<what is wrong or missing, who it affects, and how you would check it is fixed>

Flags: --priority low|medium|high|extreme · --risk low|medium|high · --assignee <login>.
File the issue only - do not implement it. Dedupe against open issues and PRs first.
Meet the ticket-level Definition of Ready in SDLC.md: the problem and who has it, the expected
outcome and how it is checked, what is out of scope, and open questions marked blocking or
non-blocking. Apply SDLC labels on creation; never add the command labels groom, autofix or spec.

label: om-spec-writing - write or review a spec to staff-engineer standard
text:
<the feature goal, or the path of an existing spec to review>

Flags: --autonomous (resolve Open Questions with documented defaults instead of stopping).
Skeleton first, then STOP at the Open Questions gate until they are answered - that gate is hard
unless --autonomous. Break the work into phases and steps that om-auto-create-pr can execute.
Every spec here also carries "Visual change expected" and "Copy" (each en key with its text;
implementation lands EN and PL in the same change, skill i18n-messages).

label: om-auto-create-pr - run a task end to end and ship a PR
text:
<the task - one sentence or several paragraphs>

Flags: --spec <ref> · --slug <kebab-case> · --skill-url <url> (repeatable, reference only) ·
--loop · --force.
Target develop, never main. Blockers: float arithmetic on any amount (docs/MONEY.md); a new i18n
key missing from EN or PL; SQL outside src/server/repos (src/server/catalog excepted); a repo
method without a tenant-isolation test; components/ui fetching data or importing from server/; a
server function whose input is not validated with Zod; generated files edited by hand instead of
pnpm generate-routes / pnpm db:generate. Never run pnpm add|remove|update - the stack is pinned
(docs/SPEC.md §3); stop with Status: blocked instead. Fast loop: pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint &&
pnpm test.

label: om-auto-create-pr-loop - long spec implementation, step by step
text:
<the multi-step task or spec to implement>

Flags: --slug <kebab-case> · --skill-url <url> (repeatable, reference only) · --force.
Use this over om-auto-create-pr only for long work needing resumability: a run folder
(PLAN/HANDOFF/NOTIFY), one lean commit per Step, a checkpoint every ~5 Steps with integration
tests and UI screenshots, the full gate at completion. Check for an existing run folder, branch or
open PR first and hand off to om-auto-continue-pr-loop rather than starting a duplicate.
The same repo gate applies as om-auto-create-pr: integer minor units everywhere, EN + PL parity,
SQL only in src/server/repos, Zod on every server-function input, generated files only via their
generators.

label: om-create-skill - author a new om skill or split an oversized one
text:
<what the skill should do, or the name of an existing skill to split>

Flags: --mode author|split (auto-detected otherwise) · --dry-run.
Match house conventions: the layering philosophy, the lint invariants, the tracker abstraction and
the cross-skill contract. Stay behind the lint + completeness gate. Repo-specific rules belong in
.ai/skills/om-<name>/SKILL.md as an extension, never as a fork of the installed skill - the
collection here is vendored in .claude/skills/om-* at a pinned SHA and is write-protected in
agent runs.

label: om-ux-shape - turn a vague feature idea into a decided direction
text:
<the idea, the product area to review, or the decided direction to detail>

No flags. Pick a mode: Shape (default), Review (an existing flow or area), or Handoff
(implementation-ready behaviour). Judge against this repo's design contract in .uxproof/ - run
om-ux-setup first if it is missing - together with DESIGN.md and docs/ACCESSIBILITY.md.
Name the riskiest assumption and how it would be tested, and define every screen state including
empty, loading and error, plus the keyboard path. AA is the gate; never widen the accessibility
claim.

label: om-integration-tests - run or write E2E tests against the live app
text:
<the scenario or suite to run or create - leave empty to run what exists>

No flags. Attach to the descriptor om-prepare-test-env wrote at .ai/qa/test-env.json; provision it
by invoking that skill if it is missing or stale. Never guess selectors or flows - explore the
running app. Use the repo's own runner (pnpm e2e, Playwright, e2e/support/). Credentials are
references: load the env file and write "$TEST_OWNER_PASSWORD" literally, never a password value -
.ai/qa/test-env.env is never read. A red console message fails a browser run. Diagnose failures
from artifacts, never from a guess.

label: om-prepare-test-env - bring the app up for QA and integration tests
text:
Flags: --mode auto|reuse|ephemeral|dev|docker|prod · --stop / --down (tear down) · --browser on|off ·
--browser-provider <name> · --force-rebuild · --regenerate.
Provisioning is .ai/scripts/test-env-up.sh and nothing else. Bind 127.0.0.1 on a free port in
3011-3020 only - 3010 is the developer's dev server (docs/agents/shared-checkout.md) - start with
E2E=1 and vite dev --strictPort, seed and verify, then write .ai/qa/test-env.json with
browser.provider playwright. No Docker - the runtime is Miniflare. .ai/scripts/ is write-protected
in agent runs: report a broken script as blocked, never patch it.

label: om-merge-buddy - report which open PRs can merge right now
text:
Report only - never merge, comment, label or edit anything.
Treat changes-requested, qa-failed, blocked, do-not-merge and in-progress as hard blocks, and with
the QA gate on, needs-qa without qa-approved - only a human sets qa-approved. An unresolved review
thread also blocks: the develop ruleset merges nothing with one open, whatever the review decision
says. For each PR that cannot merge, name exactly what it is waiting for.

label: om-review-prs - sweep every unreviewed open PR, newest first
text:
Flags: --autofix (pass it only when the sweep should also fix; by default other authors' PRs get a
verdict and a handoff, nothing more).
Skip drafts, PRs this account authored, and any PR another actor holds with in-progress - never
force-claim in a sweep. Report a claim that outlived its run instead of repairing it.

label: om-close-fixed-issues - post-merge housekeeping on the tracker
text:
--limit 50

Other flags: --since <ISO date|git ref|last-release> · --dry-run · --repo <owner>/<name>.
Close only issues a merged PR authoritatively fixed - a fixes/closes/resolves keyword or
closingIssuesReferences. Never act on a bare #N mention. do-not-close wins over everything.
Here PRs merge into develop while the default branch is main, so GitHub never auto-closes: this
run is what actually closes them. Comment, do not close, when the PR was closed unmerged or merged
into a non-base branch.

label: om-check-and-commit - run the full gate, then commit and push
text:
Run every command in validation.commands from .ai/agentic.config.json, in order: pnpm
generate-routes with a clean git diff on src/routeTree.gen.ts, pnpm db:generate with a clean git
diff on drizzle/, pnpm typecheck, pnpm lint, pnpm test, pnpm build.
The list is authoritative - do not substitute your own commands and do not skip one because it
"probably passes". A generated file is regenerated, never hand-edited. Fix and re-run until green
before publishing; never use --no-verify. Do not revert unrelated changes in the worktree. Commit
messages: Conventional Commits, in English, scope = module or plan area.

label: om-auto-update-changelog - draft the release entry as a docs PR
text:
Flags: --version <x.y.z> · --since <ISO date|git ref|last-release> · --release-ref <ref> ·
--date <YYYY-MM-DD> · --dry-run · --slug <kebab-case>.
Cover every PR merged since the last release. Honour the Supersede Credit Rule and verify every
credit against commit authorship - a carry-forward or umbrella merge credits the contributor, not
the merger. The PR itself ships through om-auto-create-pr against develop.

label: om-pipeline-retro - rank what second passes cost the pipeline
text:
Flags: --since <YYYY-MM-DD> (default 30 days ago) · --limit <n> (default 30 per state) ·
--gap-minutes <n> (default 60) · --in-progress-label.
Read-only: classify each finished run as a clean single pass, a hard recovery, loop checkpoints, or
cause not recorded, and rank the causes by wall-clock hours lost. Hand the top cause to
om-prepare-issue rather than fixing anything here. Every number you write down came from a command
whose output you read (docs/SPEC.md §7.7).

label: om-ux-setup - extract this repo's design contract into .uxproof/
text:
No arguments; read the working tree.
Capture the tokens, component registry, screen archetypes and conventions this repo actually uses,
so every later UX skill judges against THIS design system: shadcn-shaped UI on React Aria
Components, not Radix (DESIGN.md, docs/SPEC.md §4). Produce the contract only - review nothing.
Run once per repository, and again after the design system changes.

label: om-setup-agent-pipeline - reconfigure the pipeline (rarely needed)
text:
Flags: --defaults (skip the questions and write the auto-detected config).
This repo is already configured: .ai/agentic.config.json, .ai/trackers/github.md, SDLC.md,
CODE_REVIEW.md and BACKWARD_COMPATIBILITY.md all exist. Re-run only when the toolchain or the
label taxonomy changes, and report the diff before writing - do not silently overwrite the base
branch (develop), the validation gate or the label taxonomy.

label: om-apply-upgrade-notes - migrate after a skills-collection upgrade
text:
Flags: --dry-run · --tracker <name> · --browser <name> · --yes (apply purely additive changes).
Read the collection's UPGRADE_NOTES.md and re-sync the installed tracker and browser descriptors
while preserving local edits. Report every custom-provider gap rather than papering over it.
Touch only .ai/ artifacts. skills-lock.json must move in the same commit as the vendored
.claude/skills/om-* files. Never re-add a pin to skillsRepos in .ai/cezar/config.json: it is
deliberately empty, because listing a repository there lets the cockpit replace the vendored tree.

label: om-auto-fix-issue - fix or implement an issue end to end
text:
<issue number only on this line - e.g. 1234>

Read the line above as a tracker issue id, not as a problem description.
Flags: --interactive · --no-ui · --loop · --force · --slug <kebab-case>.
Remove the `autofix` label as the first tracker mutation; never add autofix, spec or groom.
A bug runs verify -> root cause -> fix -> PR -> review -> QA; a feature runs spec -> implement.
Check docs/agents/out-of-scope.md before the feature route: a request listed there is closed with
the row's ADR as the reason, never implemented.
A diff touching src/routes, src/components, src/styles or src/lib/i18n/messages is UI-touching:
om-auto-qa-pr is mandatory and the PR carries needs-qa.
Branch fix/issue-<n>-<slug> or feat/issue-<n>-<slug>, cut from origin/develop. Keep `Closes #<n>`
in the PR body - housekeeping's om-close-fixed-issues is what acts on it, since PRs merge into
develop while the default branch is main.

label: om-auto-manage-issues - groom issues to standard, implement nothing
text:
<issue number only on this line, or leave this line empty to groom a batch>

Read the line above as a tracker issue id, not as a problem description.
Flags: --limit <n> (25) · --state open|closed|all · --label <name> (-name = missing) ·
--author <login> · --relabel-only · --prep-impl / --no-prep · --write-missing-specs · --dry-run.
Never implement anything. Remove the `groom` label as the first mutation and never add a command
label. Skip any issue held by blocked, do-not-close or do-not-merge.
Map the category from .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE (bug report -> bug, enhancement -> feature,
maintenance -> refactor, Dependabot -> dependencies). Record READY_STATUS against the Definition
of Ready in SDLC.md and name what is missing. Implementation notes must name the owning module
(docs/SPEC.md §8) and flag any BACKWARD_COMPATIBILITY.md surface.

label: om-auto-write-spec - land a spec on a design-only PR
text:
<issue number only on this line, or a feature brief instead>

Flags: --slug <kebab-case> · --no-mockups · --force.
Remove the `spec` label as the first mutation; never add a command label.
The spec lands in .ai/specs/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md and carries two sections this repo requires
beyond the standard ones: "Visual change expected", and "Copy" listing each en key with its text
(implementation lands EN and PL in the same change).
Read CONTEXT.md for the vocabulary and docs/SPEC.md for the architecture the spec must respect;
an amount is integer minor units at every layer (docs/MONEY.md).
The PR is design-only: branch spec/<slug>, body `Refs #<n>`, labels review, documentation,
skip-qa, one priority and one risk. Ship no implementation on it - that is a separate run through
om-auto-implement-spec once a human merges this PR.

label: om-auto-implement-spec - build a merged spec and ship a PR
text:
<spec path, spec name, issue number, or spec-PR number - one reference on this line>

Flags: --no-ui · --loop · --force.
Resolve the reference in order: path, then name in .ai/specs/, then issue-body links, then the
spec-PR branch. If it does not resolve, stop and list the closest candidates - never guess.
The spec PR stays design-only: the implementation ships on its own PR against develop carrying
`Refs #<specPr>` and a `Source doc:` line. A new repository function ships with a tenant-isolation
case, a new money-touching write path with a money-invariants case. Finish with the review loop
and, for user-facing work, UI verification with screenshots.

label: om-auto-continue-pr - resume an open PR from its plan
text:
<PR number only on this line - e.g. 312>

Flags: --force (take over another actor's claim) · --from <phase.step> · --adopt ask|auto|off ·
--goal "<text>".
Resume from the first unchecked step of the PR's `Tracking plan:`. A PR with no plan is adopted:
reconstruct the goal from its description, comments, review feedback, linked issues and diff -
reconstruction never licenses work the diff and conversation do not support.
The repo gate still applies: integer minor units on every amount, EN + PL parity, SQL only in
src/server/repos, Zod on every server-function input, generated files only via pnpm
generate-routes / pnpm db:generate, and never pnpm add|remove|update.

label: om-auto-continue-pr-loop - resume a loop-engine PR at its next Step
text:
<PR number only on this line - e.g. 312>

Flags: --force · --from <phase.step>.
Only for a PR started by om-auto-create-pr-loop - it must carry `Tracking plan:` and
`Tracking run folder:`. If it does not, use om-auto-continue-pr instead.
Resume at the first non-done row of the run folder's PLAN.md Tasks table and keep the discipline:
one lean commit per Step, a checkpoint every ~5 Steps with integration tests and UI screenshots,
the full gate at completion. A spec-only design PR stays design-only.

label: om-auto-review-pr - review or re-review one PR
text:
<PR number only on this line - e.g. 312>

Flags: --autofix (fix -> re-review loop; required for a PR this account did not author) · --force.
Build the INHERITED finding set from list-review-threads, not list-review-comments, and keep each
thread id with its first comment id.
Reply in every thread you act on: fixed -> reply and resolve; deferred -> reply naming the
follow-up issue and resolve; declined -> reply, leave the thread open, verdict changes-requested.
The develop ruleset merges nothing with an open thread. On a non-autofix pass leave threads as you
found them and list them by path.
Blockers on the diff alone: an added @ts-ignore, @ts-expect-error or eslint-disable; an added
.skip/.only/.todo/.fixme; tests deleted without the code; a hand-edited src/routeTree.gen.ts or
drizzle/ file; a dependency change outside a dependencies PR; float arithmetic on an amount.

label: om-auto-fix-pr - drive a PR to merge-ready (never merges)
text:
<PR number only on this line - e.g. 312>

Flags: --ci-only (CI stabilization alone) · --branch <name> (only with --ci-only) ·
--max-iterations <n> (default 3) · --no-ui · --force.
Merge the latest develop first, then loop review-autofix, CI stabilization and UI verification.
The loop is not done while a review thread is open - the develop ruleset blocks the merge on one
even after an approving review. Reply and resolve threads you handled; a declined thread leaves the
verdict at changes-requested, never merge-queue.
File follow-up issues for nits rather than widening the diff. Never merge - hand off to
om-approve-merge-pr.

label: om-pr-autopilot - diagnose a PR and run whatever it needs
text:
<PR number only on this line - e.g. 312>

Flags: --dry-run (diagnose only, mutate nothing) · --confirm · --allow-merge (off by default -
the run stops at merge-ready) · --force · --max-iterations <n> (default 3).
Diagnose the PR's actual state first - unfinished plan steps, missing review, unresolved threads,
red CI, base conflicts, missing QA evidence - then dispatch the matching chain verbatim and publish
a status report. Do not add --allow-merge unless a human asked for the merge.

label: om-approve-merge-pr - approve and squash-merge one PR
text:
<PR number only on this line - e.g. 312>

No flags; add "and file a follow-up: <text>" to open one at the same time.
Refuse and report when the PR is draft, conflicting, or carries changes-requested, qa-failed,
blocked or do-not-merge, or when needs-qa lacks qa-approved - only a human sets qa-approved.
Before merging, run list-review-threads: any unresolved, non-outdated thread blocks the merge even
with an approving review and green CI, because the develop ruleset says so. Report such threads by
path and author and offer om-auto-fix-pr - never resolve them from here.
Route a fixable blocker to om-auto-fix-pr (--ci-only for red CI) rather than forcing the merge.

label: om-auto-qa-pr - verify a PR's UI in a real browser
text:
<PR number only on this line - e.g. 312>

Flags: --base <branch> · --evidence-only (default) · --self-qa-signoff · --keep-env ·
--artifacts <dir> · --force. Leave the line above empty to QA the current worktree instead.
Bring the app up with sh .ai/scripts/test-env-up.sh and read baseUrl from .ai/qa/test-env.json;
credentials are references, never values.
Evidence here is the blind A/B pair (ADR 0016): node scripts/visual/capture.mjs for each changed
route, base and head, light and dark, at 1440x900 and 360x800, plus the interaction state.
Attach them with attach-image-evidence and keep the files in .ai/qa/artifacts_*/ - never inside
the repository. Evidence only: never apply qa-approved or qa-self-verified here - a human QA
reviewer does that.

label: om-qa-buddy - a manual QA session with a runbook you test from
text:
<PR number, issue number or branch on this line - leave empty to QA the working tree>

Flags: --base <branch> (default develop) · --artifacts <dir>. Human in the loop, not a sign-off:
write the test plan first, then publish runbook.html in the artifacts directory before booting
anything and hand over its path, so the tester works through it in parallel.
Bring the app up with sh .ai/scripts/test-env-up.sh and read baseUrl from .ai/qa/test-env.json;
credentials are references, never values. Drive the UI only, never a direct API call. Cover the
changed flow in EN and PL, light and dark, at 1440x900 and 360x800, and once keyboard only.
Keep every artifact in .ai/qa/artifacts_*/ - never inside the repository. Read-only on the
tracker and on source: no comment, label, claim, commit or push; hand the verdict and the bug
files over to be posted by a human. Never mark a case passed that was not exercised.

label: om-ux-review-pr - design review of what a PR ships
text:
<PR number or branch on this line - leave empty to review the working tree>

No flags. Walk the changed screens in a real browser and perform the user's tasks - do not review
from the diff. Rank findings by user impact, and give every one four parts: the evidence, the
pattern, the trade-off and an acceptance criterion. A finding missing any part is not ready to be
said out loud; label opinions as opinions. Judge against .uxproof/ and DESIGN.md, not against
taste. Every chart needs its visually-hidden data table and a non-colour encoding (ADR 0007).
Scope guard: for a whole module, flow or product area use om-ux-shape in Review mode instead.

label: om-code-review - review a diff, branch or PR against the standards
text:
<PR number, branch, or commit range - leave empty for the current branch vs develop>

No flags. Run the validation gate, then apply the built-in checklist plus CODE_REVIEW.md,
BACKWARD_COMPATIBILITY.md and .ai/review-checklist.md, and produce severity-ranked findings with
an approve or request-changes verdict.
Blockers checkable on the diff alone: float arithmetic on an amount at any layer, a chart label
included; an added @ts-ignore, @ts-expect-error or eslint-disable; an added .skip/.only/.todo/
.fixme; tests deleted without the code; a hand-edited src/routeTree.gen.ts or drizzle/ file; a
dependency change outside a dependencies PR; a repo method without a tenant-isolation test; SQL
outside src/server/repos or src/server/catalog; a direct write to account_balances outside
src/server/ledger; an i18n key missing from EN or PL. Style smells are minor, never blockers.

label: om-verify-in-repo - is this issue real and still unfixed?
text:
<issue number only on this line - e.g. 1234>

No flags. Read-only triage gate - change nothing.
Answer with the literal NO_ACTION_NEEDED on its own line when the issue is already fixed on
develop, already claimed by someone else, already covered by an open PR, or not actually a bug.
Otherwise confirm it in 200 words or fewer and hand on to om-root-cause.

label: om-root-cause - locate the bug and the minimal change surface
text:
<issue number only on this line - e.g. 1234>

No flags. Read-only - do not implement anything.
Stop and say so if om-verify-in-repo has not confirmed this issue first.
Return the cause, the files that must change, and the proposed approach, precise enough that the
next agent does not have to re-explore the repo. Name the owning module (docs/SPEC.md §8) and flag
any BACKWARD_COMPATIBILITY.md surface the fix would touch. Next step: om-fix.

label: om-fix - implement the minimal fix plus a regression test
text:
<issue number only on this line - e.g. 1234>

No flags. Stop and report if om-root-cause has not produced an analysis for this issue.
Claim the issue first: assignee, the in-progress label, and a claim comment; release it on exit,
including on error. Implement the minimal change and add a regression test that fails without it.
Do not commit, push or open a PR - that is om-open-pr's job.
Blockers: float arithmetic on an amount; a new i18n key missing from EN or PL; SQL outside
src/server/repos; a repo method without a tenant-isolation test; components/ui fetching data or
importing from server/; a server-function input not validated with Zod; hand-edited generated
files. Never run pnpm add|remove|update - stop with Status: blocked. Gate: pnpm typecheck &&
pnpm lint && pnpm test.

label: om-open-pr - commit, push and open the labelled PR
text:
<issue number only on this line, or leave empty for a brief- or spec-driven run>

Flags: --title <text> · --plan <path> · --draft · --summary-file <path> · --handoff <next-skill> ·
{category} = bug|feature|refactor|security|dependencies|documentation.
Target develop, never main. Reuse an existing PR for this branch rather than opening a second one.
`Closes #<n>` when the PR fully implements the issue, `Refs #<n>` when it is partial or spec-only -
that line is the contract om-close-fixed-issues reads at housekeeping.
Fill the sections of .github/pull_request_template.md, the Definition of done (docs/SPEC.md §7)
included. Choose needs-qa or skip-qa from the diff surface; risk-high for src/server/auth,
src/server/repos/base.ts, src/server/billing, src/server/ledger, src/server/db/schema.ts or
drizzle/. Branch prefixes: fix/issue-<n>-<slug>, feat/issue-<n>-<slug>, spec/<slug>. Never use
--no-verify.

label: om-followup-issue-from-pr - turn a PR comment into tracked work
text:
<paste the PR or PR-comment URL on this line>

No flags. Accepts .../pull/<n>#issuecomment-<id>, .../pull/<n>#discussion_r<id>, or a plain
.../pull/<n>. Parse the repo from the URL - do not assume the current one.
Extract the actionable ask and file it against the @-mentioned person, or the PR author when
nobody is named. For a PR that only adds a design document, open the missing `Implement:` tracking
issue instead. Apply SDLC labels on creation; never add a command label.
